Those who would evaluate this documentary solely on its entertainment value are completely missing the point. This work portrays the battle using setup detail description and filming methods that take you right into the action. If you really want to know who made "Breakfast Pals" then here goes... Okay, Cartoon Films Ltd. was NOT a pseudonym for Disney nor for moonlighting Fleischer animators (including Dave Tendlar ;o)). The company was in reality the final incarnation of the cartoon studio of the great Ub Iwerks (the designer of Mickey Mouse). By the time this was made, Iwerks was not really wanting to direct, so it was likely directed by Paul Fennell (formerly of Harman-Ising, Schlesinger/Warners, Fleischer and Disney), and supposedly animated by Rudy Zamora and Ed Benedict. rv: This is a collection of largely home movies from the 40s and 50s of life in and around Detroit---one of the world's greatest cities in those days and, during WW II, perhaps the world's most important. We see downtown streets thronged with people; automobile plants; the Vernor's Ginger Ale plant (Vernor's was, and is, the most distinctive ginger ale ever made); vibrant neighborhoods; grand movie houses (including United Artists on the day "Anatomy of A Murder" premiered when director Otto Preminger and star Lee Remick made personal appearances); parks, inluding Belle Isle in the Detroit River--

60 minute travelogue on Detroit, using mostly silent film (though sound bits due turn up from time to time). This film showcases the many historical facades of Detroit, and it should be interesting to most people, Detroitese or not. I myself got suckered in by the massive billboards on display. bee-yoo-ti-full! Something for everyone!
